summary: Bokar Rinpoche (1940–2004) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Kalu Rinpoche from around 1967 to 1989, taught Shenpen Hookham and Lama Palden Drolma, and held a post at Bokar Ngedon Choekhor Ling Monastery (~1984–2004).

Bong Seok Joo specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley, and earned a PhD at Princeton University under doctoral supervisor Stephen F. Teiser, also studying with Jacqueline I. Stone and others.

Bongkil Chung is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner. He held posts at Florida International University from 1991 to 1992 and as professor of philosophy in 2012.

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov (1900–1981) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky from around 1920 to 1925 and held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts from circa 1930 to 1937.

Brad Warner (born 1964) is a specialist in Buddhist and religious studies. He attended Wadsworth High School and Kent State University (~1982–1987), and studied under traditional teacher Tim McCarthy as well as Gudo Wafu Nishijima.

Bradford Lyman Phillips specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Naropa University, earned degrees at the University of Virginia (BA, PhD) and Harvard University (MTS), and was supervised by David Germano and advised by Cecil Y. Lang.
Bradley L. Herling works in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held posts as Assistant Director at Boston University and at Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

Braj Basi Lal (1921–2022) studied at the University of Allahabad. In Indology and archaeology, he served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972), professor at Jiwaji University (~1972–1976), and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson (born 1978) specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and a habilitation at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich, holding posts at Oxford, SOAS, Munich, and Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.
Brandon J. Harwood is a scholar of religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Louisville (attested 2015) under advisor Patrick Pranke.

Brendan S. Gillon works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1980–1985) and served as Associate Professor in the Department of Linguistics at McGill University around 1992.

Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and religious studies. He studied at Vanderbilt University and Kyoto University, taught at Shiga and Kwansei Gakuin universities, was a fellow at Otani and Kyoto universities, and held philosophy posts at Loyola University Maryland.
Brian Bocking is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Leeds, where he studied under Michael Pye.

Brian D. Ruppert (born 1962) specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, having studied under Willis Stoesz. He held a post at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1999–2018) before joining Bates College around 2018 as Kazushige Hirasawa Professor.

Brian Daizen Victoria (born 1939) works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Nebraska Wesleyan, Komazawa (MA), and Temple (PhD) universities, and held posts as professor at Antioch University (~2005–2012) and at the University of Adelaide (2011).
Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University by 2005 under the supervision of György Kara.

Brian Houghton Hodgson (1800–1894) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar. After studies including Haileybury, East India Company College, and Fort William College, he served as Assistant Resident (1820) and British Resident in Nepal (~1833–1843).

Brian J. Nichols works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He attended the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and earned a PhD at Rice University under Anne Carolyn Klein (attested 2011).

Bridget Allchin (1927–2017) was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Cape Town (~1944–1947). She founded the European Association of South Asian Archaeology and Art in 1970 and held a post at Wolfson College.
Brigitte Marschall (born 1957) studied at the University of Vienna (~1976–1982), where she later became a professor around 1997. She also taught Mungunchimeg Batmunkh.
